days.notes: No change to the tour; date shifted by the new day count.
No change to the tour; date shifted by the new day count.
days.stay: The Inn at Cold Foot Camp

days.notes: No change to the tour; date shifted by the new day count.
No change to the tour; date shifted by the new day count.
No change to the tour; date shifted by the new day count.
Rest day.
Renamed only (old S1D6).
Renamed only (old S1D7).
Renamed only (old S1D8).
Renamed only (old S1D9).

Replaces your old S1D10 (Haines Junction camp to Whitehorse). Alaska Hwy to the Klondike Hwy junction NW of Whitehorse, then north and 10 km up Takhini Hot Springs Rd. Campground beside the springs. REST DAY TOMORROW.
days.stay: Campground beside Eclipse Nordic Hot Springs

days.notes: Rest day.

Replaces your old S1D11 (Whitehorse to Johnson's Crossing). Back out to the Alaska Hwy, resupply in Whitehorse, then your existing line to Johnson's Crossing. Next: S1D14 Johnson's Crossing to Rancheria Lodge.
Merges old S1D14 and S1D15. Alaska Hwy through Teslin, a short dip into BC, Swift River, then Rancheria Lodge (open year-round, camping, cafe). Long day but no big passes.

Merges old S1D15 and S1D16. Rancheria Falls trail early, then Junction 37 (Nugget City: gas, restaurant, camping). Watson Lake is 13 mi east if you need a full grocery store. South on the Cassiar to Boya Lake.
Jade City (jade shop, small store) about 22 mi in. Longest gap between fuel/services on the Cassiar is Watson Lake to Dease Lake. REST DAY TOMORROW.
Rest day.
Over Gnat Pass to Iskut (store, fuel), then Kinaskan Lake campground.
Intermittent gravel sections between Kinaskan and the Bell-Irving River. Bell 2 Lodge at the end.

days.terrain: Rolling, long descent to sea level
days.notes: Down the Cassiar to Meziadin Junction, then west on 37A past Bear Glacier to Stewart. Overnight only (add a day here if you want Hyder and the glaciers).
No services at Cranberry Junction. Plan a wild camp and carry dinner and breakfast from Stewart or Meziadin Junction.
days.stay: Wild camp (no services at Cranberry Junction)

days.notes: Down to Kitwanga, onto the Yellowhead (Hwy 16) east through New Hazelton to Smithers. REST DAY TOMORROW.
Rest day.
Yellowhead through Telkwa and Houston.
Past Fraser Lake. Beaumont Provincial Park on Fraser Lake is a nice lunch stop.
Resupply and bike shop stop in Prince George at mile 60, then 40 mi east to the Purden Lake campground (only provincial campground between Prince George and Mount Robson).

days.terrain: Rolling, gradual climb up the Fraser valley
days.notes: Very few services until McBride. Dome Creek is tiny.
Past Mount Robson (visitor centre views) and over Yellowhead Pass, the lowest pass through the Rockies, into Jasper National Park. REST DAY TOMORROW.
Rest day.
Icefields Parkway south. Athabasca and Sunwapta Falls on the way. Wilcox and Icefield campgrounds near the Icefield Centre.
days.stay: Wilcox / Icefield campgrounds near the Icefield Centre

days.terrain: One big climb (Bow Summit), otherwise downhill
days.notes: Merges old S1D32 and S1D33. Down to Saskatchewan Crossing, up Bow Summit, Lake Louise, then the Bow Valley Parkway to Banff. Evening soak at Banff Upper Hot Springs.
Back to Castle Junction, then Hwy 93 south through Kootenay National Park. You roll through Sinclair Canyon right past the pools. REST DAY TOMORROW.
Rest day.

days.terrain: Rolling, then climb to Rogers Pass
days.notes: Flat Columbia Valley to Golden, then the Trans-Canada over Rogers Pass. Heavy truck traffic, snow sheds. Camp in Glacier National Park near the summit.
days.stay: Camp in Glacier National Park near the summit

days.notes: Descend to Revelstoke, Hwy 23 south to Shelter Bay, free ferry to Galena Bay, then south to Halcyon. REST DAY TOMORROW.
Rest day.
Merges old S1D39 and most of S1D40. Hwy 23 to Nakusp, Hwy 6 along the Arrow Lakes to Fauquier, free Needles ferry, then over Monashee Pass to Cherryville.
Merges the end of old S1D40 with S1D41. Lumby and Vernon, then down the Okanagan through Kelowna, Peachland and Summerland.
Hwy 3A to Keremeos, then Hwy 3 up the Similkameen valley.
Through Manning Park, then the long descent to Hope.
Hwy 7 on the north side of the Fraser (quieter than Hwy 1) through Agassiz, Mission and Maple Ridge. Rest days Jul 29-30 in Vancouver.
Rest day.
Rest day.
Renamed only (old S1D29).
Renamed only (old S1D30).
Rest day.
No ferry: south to Tacoma, over the Tacoma Narrows Bridge path, Gig Harbor, Belfair, then SR-106 along the south shore of Hood Canal to Potlatch State Park
US-101 up the west side of Hood Canal through Hoodsport, Brinnon and Quilcene, then Sequim and the Olympic Discovery Trail into Port Angeles. REST DAY TOMORROW

Rest day, optional outing. OPTIONAL rest-day outing, ride unloaded. Out to the Elwha, park at Madison Falls, ride the closed Olympic Hot Springs Road (bypass trail around the washout) to Boulder Creek trailhead, then hike to the springs. Bikes are not allowed past the trailhead. Miles are round trip
US-101 along Lake Crescent (curvy, no shoulder in places), Forks, then the 18-mile Hoh River Road into the rain forest. Camp at Hoh campground
Back to 101, Ruby Beach, Kalaloch beaches, then Lake Quinault
Aberdeen, Raymond, South Bend, then along Willapa Bay to Ilwaco

days.terrain: Rolling, one climb over the Coast Range
days.notes: Astoria-Megler Bridge, Astoria, Seaside and Cannon Beach, then US-26 inland to Stub Stewart State Park
Short day so you have the afternoon in Portland. Banks-Vernonia Trail to Banks, then Hillsboro and Beaverton into the city
Willamette Valley via Champoeg, Salem, Independence and Corvallis (much of it on the Willamette Valley Scenic Bikeway)
McKenzie Highway (OR-126) upriver to Blue River, then Aufderheide Drive (FR 19) past Cougar Reservoir. Camp at Cougar Crossing campground, the closest to the springs. REST DAY TOMORROW

days.from: Terwilliger Hot Springs, camp Cougar Crossing
days.to: Terwilliger Hot Springs, camp Cougar Crossing
days.stay: Terwilliger Hot Springs, camp Cougar Crossing

days.notes: Aufderheide Drive south over the summit to Westfir and Oakridge, soak at McCredie (short walk from Hwy 58), then OR-58 over Willamette Pass
US-97 south to Chemult, OR-138 to the North Entrance, then East Rim Drive clockwise past Cleetwood, Cloudcap and Kerr Notch to Mazama Village. Water only at Rim Village and Mazama Village
OR-62 down the Rogue through Union Creek, Prospect and Shady Cove, then Medford, Jacksonville and OR-238 to Grants Pass
US-199 through Cave Junction, then down the Smith River canyon past Jedediah Smith Redwoods to Crescent City
US-101 through Del Norte Coast Redwoods and Klamath, then the Newton B. Drury Scenic Parkway to Elk Prairie. REST DAY TOMORROW
Highway 1 down the coast via Pacifica, Devil's Slide trail, Half Moon Bay, Pescadero and Davenport
Around Monterey Bay (Monterey Bay Coastal Recreation Trail where Hwy 1 is freeway), Monterey, Carmel, Point Lobos, Bixby Bridge, to Pfeiffer Big Sur
Highway 1 south past McWay Falls and Esalen. Replaces the old 'Can't create' day. Optional Esalen public night soak (1-3 a.m.) if you sleep nearby

Hwy 5 south along the Sea of Cortez to Puertecitos (90 km south of San Felipe). No gas in Puertecitos. Camp at the campo; the fee covers the tidal hot springs. Soak at mid-tide; low tide can be too hot. Check a tide table.
Second half of your old San Felipe to Rancho Grande day. Short day after the morning soak. Alfonsina's at Gonzaga Bay.
Paved Hwy 1 along Bahia Concepcion (Santispac, El Requeson) then inland to Loreto. Replaces the dirt Comondu day.

days.terrain: Big climb (Sierra de la Giganta), then flat
days.notes: Hwy 1 south, then over the Sierra de la Giganta to Ciudad Insurgentes and Ciudad Constitucion.

Replaces your old El Centenario to La Paz day. Through La Paz and up the coast road to Pichilingue. Saturday sailing: foot passenger check-in 17:30, departs 19:00, arrives Mazatlan 09:00. Balandra and Tecolote beaches are just past the terminal if you have time. Ferry: Pichilingue to Mazatlan, Saturday, check-in 17:30, departs 19:00, arrives 09:00
Hwy 544 into the Sierra (renovated road) via Las Palmas, La Estancia and San Sebastian del Oeste, a Pueblo Magico, to Mascota.
Hwy 70 through Atenguillo and Mixtlan. Touring cyclists report 124 km with 2,100 m of climbing.
Via Tala into Guadalajara. REST DAY TOMORROW.
East through Zapotlanejo, Tepatitlan and San Juan de los Lagos.

days.terrain: Rolling, climb over Sierra de Lobos
days.notes: Into north Leon, then the Leon-San Felipe road over the Sierra de Lobos. Stay north of Leon: do NOT ride Hwy 45 or 45D toward Silao (US advisory restricts travel on or south of 45D).
Fed 51 to Dolores Hidalgo, then Hwy 110 over the Sierra de Santa Rosa into Guanajuato city (avoids Silao).

Back over the Sierra de Santa Rosa to Dolores Hidalgo, then south toward San Miguel. Thermal parks around km 10 (Escondido Place, La Gruta): day pass, arrive by early afternoon. Overnight in San Miguel (no rest day).
Hwy 111 to Queretaro's historic center, then east to the Pena de Bernal monolith.
Hwy 120 into the Sierra Gorda: Ezequiel Montes, Cadereyta, Vizarron, over Pinal de Amoles and down to Jalpan (Franciscan mission).
Short day: Landa de Matamoros, then the descent into Xilitla. Afternoon at Las Pozas surrealist gardens.
Down to Hwy 85 at Axtla, north through Tancanhuitz to Aquismon. Sotano de las Golondrinas: swifts at dusk and dawn.
Short day into Ciudad Valles, base for Tamul and Micos. REST DAY TOMORROW (Tamul boat or Micos).
South on Hwy 85, the original Pan-American Highway.
Hwy 85 climbs out of the jungle into the Sierra Madre Oriental via Chapulhuacan.

days.terrain: Big climbs, steep descent at the end
days.notes: Hwy 85 to Zimapan and Ixmiquilpan, then via Cardonal and the steep road down into the Tolantongo canyon. Cash only at Tolantongo (no ATMs). Overnight: soak in the evening and early morning, then ride on. Entry is charged per day, so a morning soak may need a second day ticket.

days.terrain: Big climb out of the canyon, then rolling
days.notes: Climb out via Cardonal, Ixmiquilpan, Actopan, Pachuca.

days.terrain: Rolling, heavy traffic at the end
days.notes: Via Teotihuacan (stop at the pyramids), then into Mexico City. Ride the city stretch early. REST DAYS (4) in Mexico City (Oct 16-19).
Short day out of the city through Chalco. Sunday morning traffic is lightest if you can shift it.
Paved up to the pass between Popocatepetl and Iztaccihuatl, rough dirt on the way down. Check the volcano alert before you go.
Hwy 140 east via Amozoc, Acajete, Nopalucan and Oriental to Perote, under the Cofre de Perote.
Down off the plateau through Las Vigas into Xalapa, then to Coatepec, a coffee-country Pueblo Magico. REST DAY TOMORROW (Coatepec and Xico).
Through Xico and Teocelo, south via Cosautlan and Huatusco to Cordoba, then up to Orizaba below Pico de Orizaba.

days.terrain: Mostly downhill, then flat and hot
days.notes: Down past Cordoba into the lowlands via La Tinaja and Tierra Blanca to Tuxtepec. Ride in daylight; start early for the heat.
Short day up the river valley on Hwy 175 (46 km). Swim in the river; tomorrow is the big climb.
Hwy 175, the Tuxtepec road, from jungle to pine forest over the Sierra Juarez to Ixtlan (108 km). Biggest single climb in Mexico for you. REST DAY TOMORROW (Ixtlan / Capulalpan).

days.terrain: Climb over La Cumbre, then long descent
days.notes: Past Guelatao, over La Cumbre Ixtepeji (about 2,740 m) and down into Oaxaca. Oaxaca days Oct 31 - Nov 2 (Dia de Muertos).
Hwy 175 south through Ocotlan and Ejutla.
Short on purpose: big climb into cloud forest. Sleep in San Jose del Pacifico.
Hwy 175 down to Pochutla, then the coast to Zipolite. Beach days Nov 6-8 (S3D142-144).
Hwy 200 east along the Oaxaca coast via Pochutla and Huatulco to the surf village of Barra de la Cruz. Few shops on this stretch; carry food and water

days.terrain: Mostly flat, hot, wind possible near Salina Cruz
days.notes: Hwy 200 to Salina Cruz, then Hwy 185 to Tehuantepec. Start early. Check the forecast tonight: a cold front in the Gulf of Mexico means a north wind through the Isthmus

days.stay: Tehuantepec (wind buffer: wait here if the north wind is blowing; if calm, ride to Matias Romero today and keep the spare day)

days.terrain: Rolling, exposed to the north wind
days.notes: The windy stretch: Hwy 190 to Juchitan and La Ventosa, then Hwy 185 north through the Chivela pass to Matias Romero. Only ride it on a calm day; leave at first light
Hwy 185 north via Palomares and Jesus Carranza to Acayucan
East past Cosoleacaque and Minatitlan (industrial; ride through, do not linger)
Hwy 180 via Cardenas into Villahermosa. REST DAY TOMORROW (Parque-Museo La Venta, Olmec heads)
North to the Gulf coast at Frontera
Hwy 180 along the Gulf via Atasta and the Zacatal bridge onto Isla del Carmen
Hwy 180 along the Gulf via Isla Aguada and Sabancuy
Coast road into Campeche; afternoon in the walled old town
Inland via Hopelchen and Bolonchen along the Ruta Puuc (Kabah) to Uxmal
Via Muna. REST DAY TOMORROW
East via Chichen Itza (stop at the ruins), then Valladolid; cenotes everywhere
Via Coba (ruins and lagoon) to Tulum. REST DAY TOMORROW
Hwy 307 south past Muyil and the Sian Ka'an edge
Hwy 307 to Bacalar; swim in the Laguna de los Siete Colores
BORDER DAY (Mexico to Belize). Past Chetumal to the Subteniente Lopez / Santa Elena crossing, then Corozal and Orange Walk. Keep your Mexico tourist-fee receipt; Belize charges no entry fee
Northern Hwy south, the Burrell Boom cut-off to skip Belize City, then the Western Hwy through Belmopan (the capital; lunch stop) to San Ignacio. Long day; do not ride between towns after dark
BORDER DAY (Belize to Guatemala). Benque Viejo to Melchor de Mencos (Belize land departure fee about US$20), then west to Flores. REST DAY TOMORROW (Tikal)
CA-13 south. Ride in daylight
CA-13 to Rio Dulce and its big bridge
South to La Ruidosa, then CA-9 west along the Motagua valley. Busy truck road; ride in daylight
CA-9 via El Rancho and Sanarate up to the capital. Stay in Zona 10 or 4; avoid Zona 18 and Villa Nueva
Over the hill to Antigua. REST DAY TOMORROW
Via Chimaltenango, Tecpan and Los Encuentros, then the steep drop to Lake Atitlan. REST DAY TOMORROW

days.terrain: Big climbs (850 m out of Pana, high point about 2,850 m)
days.notes: Back up to the Interamericana, via Nahuala and Cuatro Caminos into Xela (last stretch busy and rough)
Via Almolonga and Zunil, then 8 km up the access road. Overnight in a bungalow (about Q190 per person, entry included) for after-hours soaking. Cash only
Down to Zunil, then the road south through Santa Maria de Jesus and El Palmar to Retalhuleu and Mazatenango
CA-2 east along the Pacific plain via Escuintla. Ride straight through in daylight
BORDER DAY (Guatemala to El Salvador). Via Chiquimulilla to Ciudad Pedro de Alvarado / La Hachadura, then the coast to Acajutla

days.terrain: Rolling coast with short steep climbs
days.notes: The Litoral (CA-2) along the cliffs via Los Cobanos, Mizata and El Zonte. Narrow tunnels with little shoulder: lights on, wait for a gap in traffic
Via La Libertad and Santa Tecla up to the capital. REST DAY TOMORROW
CA-1 east via Cojutepeque and San Vicente junction
BORDER DAY (El Salvador to Honduras). Via Santa Rosa de Lima to El Amatillo (Honduras entry about US$3 cash; online customs form), then Nacaome and San Lorenzo on the Gulf of Fonseca
BORDER DAY (Honduras to Nicaragua). Via Choluteca to Guasaule (Nicaragua online entry form filed in advance; US$10 cash), then Somotillo
Via Chinandega, under the volcano chain
Via La Paz Centro and Nagarote, through the edge of Managua without stopping, then Masaya. REST DAYS (2) in Granada, over Christmas
South via Nandaime to Rivas and San Jorge, then the ferry to Moyogalpa (about 1 hour; departures roughly every 30-90 min from 7:00 to 17:45; C$50 plus about US$1 port tax)

days.terrain: Rolling, some rough road on the Maderas side
days.notes: Unloaded loop day: around Volcan Concepcion via Altagracia, out to Playa Santo Domingo and Balgue on the Maderas side, back via Charco Verde
BORDER DAY (Nicaragua to Costa Rica). Early ferry to San Jorge (first boats 5:30-7:00), ride via Rivas to Penas Blancas, then La Cruz
Interamericana via Liberia and Bagaces
Interamericana south to Rio Lagarto, then up via Guacimal to Santa Elena / Monteverde cloud forest. REST DAY TOMORROW

days.terrain: Hilly; the Monteverde to Tilaran road may be partly unpaved
days.notes: Down to Tilaran, around Lake Arenal via Nuevo Arenal and the dam to La Fortuna under Arenal volcano
South via Chachagua and the climb to San Ramon
Back roads via Palmares, Grecia, Alajuela and Heredia; avoid the Interamericana (Ruta 1) near San Jose. REST DAYS (2): sloths at Toucan Rescue Ranch near Heredia (book ahead)
Santa Ana and Ciudad Colon to Atenas, the old road (Ruta 3) to Orotina, then Tarcoles (crocodile bridge) to Jaco. Do not ride Ruta 27
Costanera Sur (Ruta 34) via Parrita to Quepos and Manuel Antonio (sloths in the park)
Costanera Sur via Dominical to Uvita (Whale's Tail)
Via Ojochal and Palmar Norte, then the Interamericana to Ciudad Neily
BORDER DAY (Costa Rica to Panama). Paso Canoas, then the Interamericana to David
Up to the coffee highlands. REST DAY TOMORROW
Back to David, then the Interamericana east (busy for about 15 km, wide shoulder after about 30 km)
Interamericana via Tole
Interamericana via Divisa and Aguadulce
Via Anton and Rio Hato to the Pacific beaches at Coronado

days.terrain: Rolling, heavy traffic at the end
days.notes: Via Chame, Capira and La Chorrera. Bridge of the Americas is officially closed to bikes; arrive on a Sunday morning if you can. REST DAYS (2)
East on the Interamericana via Tocumen and Chepo to El Llano, the start of the Carti road. Stock up on cash: no ATMs ahead until Necocli

The El Llano to Carti road over the divide into Guna Yala (entry fee at the checkpoint). Sleep near Carti port for the morning boat. Komoot shows 25 ft up, an elevation-model artifact over its off-grid segment; the GPX showed 2,125 ft of gain. Elevation in this row is the GPX figure.
San Blas Adventures day 1: Carti, boat into the islands.
San Blas Adventures day 2: island hopping.
San Blas Adventures day 3: island hopping.
San Blas Adventures day 4: Puerto Obaldia (Panama exit stamp), Sapzurro, Capurgana (Colombia entry stamp at immigration office).
San Blas Adventures day 5 ends in Capurgana; boat to Necocli (end of Section 4).
Coast road via Arboletes. UK advises against non-essential travel in the Uraba region (Necocli, Arboletes): ride straight through in daylight.
Via San Bernardo del Viento and Lorica to the Gulf of Morrosquillo.
Via Tolu, San Onofre and Maria la Baja. REST DAYS (2) in Cartagena.
Via al Mar along the Caribbean. REST DAY TOMORROW: Museo de Arte Moderno de Barranquilla.
Across the Isla de Salamanca road (mangroves and sea) and Cienaga. REST DAY TOMORROW (Tayrona).
Up into the Sierra Nevada foothills: birds, waterfalls, coffee farms.
Back down via Cienaga, south on Ruta 45.
Ruta 45 via Bosconia.
Via Pelaya and Tamalameque to the Magdalena at El Banco.
Over the bridge onto the island (no ferry from this side). REST DAY TOMORROW (UNESCO colonial river town).
Back to El Banco, then south to Aguachica.

days.terrain: Flat, then a big climb at the end (long day)
days.notes: South on Ruta 45 via San Alberto, then up via Lebrija to Bucaramanga.
Down into and out of the Chicamocha canyon (national park, viewpoints), through San Gil to Barichara. REST DAY TOMORROW.
Via Socorro and Oiba on Ruta 45A.
Via Moniquira. REST DAY TOMORROW.
Via Chiquinquira, Ubate and Zipaquira (Salt Cathedral) into the capital. REST DAYS (6): MAMBO (modern art), Museo Botero, Gold Museum, Monserrate.
Down the Ruta 50/60 from 2,600 m to the warm valley.
Into the Magdalena valley at Honda (colonial river port).
Ruta 45 then Ruta 60 toward Medellin; Rio Claro nature reserve (marble canyon). REST DAY TOMORROW.
Ruta 60 up via San Luis and Cocorna into the Antioquia highlands.
El Penol rock and the colorful town of Guatape.
Via Rionegro. REST DAYS (6): MAMM (modern art), Comuna 13, Plaza Botero.
South via Caldas and the Alto de Minas.
Ruta 25 via Irra and Neira up to Manizales.
Short day to the hot springs above Santa Rosa de Cabal. Soak tonight and in the morning, then ride on.
Via Pereira to Salento. REST DAY TOMORROW (Cocora valley wax palms).

days.terrain: Long descent, then flat and hot
days.notes: Via Armenia and La Tebaida into the Cauca valley. Rural Valle del Cauca is a US Level 4 area: daylight only, ride straight through, stop only in towns.
Via Buga and Palmira. REST DAYS (2) in Cali.
Panamericana south via Santander de Quilichao and Piendamo. Rural Cauca is a US Level 4 area: daylight only, no stops outside towns. REST DAY TOMORROW in Popayan.
Up to the Coconuco hot springs (natural, community-run). Soak tonight and in the morning.

days.terrain: Huge climb over the paramo, long unpaved stretches
days.notes: Ruta 20 via Paletara and the Purace paramo, down via Isnos to San Agustin. This avoids the Panamericana past El Bordo. REST DAY TOMORROW: San Agustin Archaeological Park.

days.terrain: Rolling, then descent to the Amazon foothills
days.notes: Back via Pitalito, then Ruta 45 south to Mocoa. The Fin del Mundo waterfall hike is just outside town if you have the legs.

days.terrain: Huge climb on dirt (Trampolin de la Muerte)
days.notes: The Mocoa to San Francisco road: unpaved, narrow, cliff-edge, landslide-prone. Daylight only.
Past Laguna de la Cocha into Pasto.
Panamericana south; Las Lajas sanctuary just outside Ipiales.
BORDER DAY (Colombia to Ecuador) at Rumichaca, then Tulcan and San Gabriel.

days.terrain: Big descent into the Chota valley and climb out
days.notes: Via Ibarra. REST DAY TOMORROW (market, Laguna Cuicocha).
Across the equator near Cayambe to the Casa de Ciclistas in Tumbaco (store the bike here for Galapagos).
Chaquinan trail and into the capital. REST DAYS (4): Capilla del Hombre and Guayasamin's house (modern art), old town.

days.stay: Galapagos (excursion day 1 of 9, Quito to Quito)
Galapagos (excursion day 2 of 9, Quito to Quito)
Galapagos (excursion day 3 of 9, Quito to Quito)
Galapagos (excursion day 4 of 9, Quito to Quito)
Galapagos (excursion day 5 of 9, Quito to Quito)
Galapagos (excursion day 6 of 9, Quito to Quito)
Galapagos (excursion day 7 of 9, Quito to Quito)
Galapagos (excursion day 8 of 9, Quito to Quito)
Galapagos (excursion day 9 of 9, Quito to Quito)

days.notes: South past the volcanoes.

days.terrain: Rolling, some dirt in the park
days.notes: Through Cotopaxi National Park.
Via Pujili and Zumbahua to the Quilotoa crater lake.
Back via Zumbahua and Pujili, then south.
Banos and its cheap municipal hot springs. REST DAY TOMORROW.
Ruta de las Cascadas (Pailon del Diablo) down to the Amazon. Then 3 days at a Puyo-area jungle lodge.
Back up the Ruta de las Cascadas.
Via Penipe, under Tungurahua and Chimborazo.
Panamericana south past Guamote.
Via Chunchi; Ingapirca ruins nearby.
Via Azogues. REST DAY TOMORROW: UNESCO old town, or Cajas National Park.
Panamericana south via Cumbe and the Tinajillas pass.
Via Saraguro.
REST DAY TOMORROW.
South via Valladolid toward the La Balsa border.
To Zumba, the last town before Peru.

days.terrain: Rough dirt to the border, then paved
days.notes: BORDER DAY (Ecuador to Peru) at La Balsa. Short day on purpose.
South to Jaen.

days.terrain: Rolling, then climbing up the Utcubamba valley
days.notes: Via Bagua Grande.
Short ride to the village below Gocta waterfall (771 m). REST DAY TOMORROW: hike to the falls.
Up the valley to Chachapoyas.
Down the Utcubamba to the Kuelap cable car. REST DAY TOMORROW: Kuelap fortress.
Up the valley to Leymebamba (mummy museum).

days.terrain: Huge climb (Calla Calla, about 3,600 m), then huge descent
days.notes: Over the pass and down into the Maranon canyon.
Out of the Maranon canyon.
To Cajamarca. REST DAY TOMORROW: Banos del Inca hot springs.
South via San Marcos.
Marcahuamachuco ruins nearby.

days.terrain: Climb, then a huge descent to the coast
days.notes: Ruta 10 west via Shiran to Trujillo. REST DAY TOMORROW: Chan Chan (adobe city) and Huanchaco.
Panamericana south. Komoot would not route the coastal Panamericana (PE-1N); the saved tour is a 226 mi inland route via Simbal/Quiruvilca — needs review
Panamericana.
Ruta 14 inland toward Huaraz.

days.terrain: Huge climb (Punta Callan, about 4,200 m), then descent
days.notes: Over the Cordillera Negra to Huaraz. REST DAYS (3): acclimatize, Laguna 69, Monterrey hot springs.
South up the Callejon de Huaylas via Recuay.
Down to Pativilca and Barranca.
Panamericana south.
Panamericana via Chancay. Komoot would not use the coastal line; the saved tour is a 114 mi inland route — needs review
Into Lima (Miraflores/Barranco). Ride early. REST DAYS (6, including a weekend): MALI and MAC Lima (modern art), food.

Panamericana Sur. Komoot avoids the Panamericana Sur; the saved tour is a 361 mi inland route and the Asia endpoint was moved ~3 km to a mapped road (original point is not on a known road in Komoot) — needs review
Via Chincha. REST DAY TOMORROW: Ballestas Islands (sea lions, penguins). Start moved to a mapped road near Asia (original start point is not on a known road in Komoot)
Via Ica to the desert oasis.
Via Palpa; the Nazca Lines viewing tower is on the road. REST DAY TOMORROW.
The Andes climb toward Puquio; vicuna reserve at the top.
Across the puna.
Remote: carry food and water.
Down to the Pachachaca valley.
Down the valley and up to Abancay. REST DAY TOMORROW after a week of high riding.
Over the pass to Curahuasi.
Via Limatambo. REST DAYS (2): Cusco, Rainbow Mountain or the Sacred Valley.
South up the Vilcanota valley via Urcos.

days.terrain: Climb over La Raya pass (about 4,330 m)
days.notes: Via Sicuani.
Via Ayaviri across the altiplano.
To Lake Titicaca. REST DAY TOMORROW (Uros floating islands).
